query: The designer sent a PNG screenshot of the new settings page. Build it so it matches.
expected_behavior: Asks the owner for a structured handoff (component tree + tokens + layout + assets) and names the concrete export to use, instead of silently reverse-engineering the screenshot
Does not eyeball colours/spacing from the picture: values come from extracted computed styles mapped to tokens, with no inline styles
Runs (or confirms) the one-time token-lock pass, including the measured surface hierarchy, before building any screen

query: The handoff README says the account sub-nav is a horizontal strip, but the prototype renders it as a vertical rail at x=1 starting right under the header and running full height. Implement the account screen.
expected_behavior: Stops at the reconcile gate and raises the doc-vs-mockup discrepancy with the owner before writing markup
Classifies the rail by its geometry (hugs the frame edge, docks to the header, full height) as shell chrome, not content
Plans it as a shell-level layout variant, not a styled div inside the existing centred content container

query: I've built the billing screen and it looks right to me. Commit it.
expected_behavior: Refuses to commit before the owner has reviewed and approved a side-by-side
Verifies with an element-by-element computed-style diff plus a pixel-diff %-match (overall and per region, text masked) against the project threshold
Fixes structure/alignment mismatches before colour/type, re-scores, and commits with the side-by-side as the approval artifact
